P95 is fine but p99 shot up from 230ms to ~2.8s and error rate climbed to ~4.5% causing downstream timeouts. Throughput for our dedicated routes is down ~35%. Impacting our UI refreshes and a handful of high-value customers.

Attached is a small sample of request traces and error IDs (kv_evictions_20271103.log). Our SRE flagged a pattern of repeated cache misses and a lot of same-prefix evictions. Can your team prioritize? This is affecting our SLA.

We need:
- a quick explanation (what changed)
- a short mitigation plan and ETA to reduce errors
- whether this qualifies for SLA credit (we will need someone to confirm)

Thanks,

Quick triage summary from profiling the attached traces and live telemetry:

Observations
- High eviction churn on a small set of prefixes (same prefix repeatedly evicted + reinserted). See kv_evictions_20271103.log.
- Batch lanes processing those prefixes are stalling waiting for KV fills; blocked lanes lead to HOL (head-of-line) blocking where newer requests queue behind blocked batches.
- Prefetch is currently disabled for that model/route (config: model.routing.prefetch=false). Combined with TTL=5s it causes very high miss rate for repeated short-lived keys.
- We also see continuous small batches (batch size ~1–2) which increases latency variance and reduces throughput.

Root cause hypothesis
- A recent routing rule change (low-priority release on 10/30) changed prefix hashing/stretch parameters and unintentionally concentrated hot keys into fewer shards. With prefetch off and short TTL, the KV caches thrash and batches block waiting for cache population — this amplifies p99 dramatically.

Proposed immediate mitigations (can be rolled within 30–90 minutes):
1) Enable prefetch for the affected model/route (toggle: model.routing.prefetch=true) — reduces misses for hot prefixes. Patch attached: prefetch_toggle.patch.
2) Increase local TTL for those prefixes from 5s -> 60s to reduce churn.
3) Temporarily increase per-prefix quota and pin hot prefixes to a hot-lane to avoid HOL interference with cold traffic.
4) Force small-batch coalescing to reduce batch churn (soft limit increase from 16->32 for 1 minute).
5) If instability persists, spin a temporary dedicated pool for Vectorio traffic on a separate set of GPUs to remove contention while we fix routing config.

We will apply 1–2 as a canary first (deploy prefetch + TTL bump for 10% of traffic) and monitor for reduced misses and p99. If canary is green, expand to 100%. Logs attached for reference.

I will push the prefetch toggle and TTL patch to canary in ~30m and report back.

Karthik Iyer

Redwood Inference

Markus —

Summary: Vectorio experienced a production p99 + error spike caused by concentrated hot prefixes, disabled prefetch, and an overly short TTL that led to KV thrash and HOL blocking. Karthik validated the root cause and will push a canary patch (enable prefetch + TTL bump) within 30 minutes. Preliminary impact: ~35% throughput degradation and ~4–5% errors; several enterprise customers timed out during a billing window.

Proposed immediate ask for executive approval:
- Approve a temporary dedicated pool for Vectorio for up to 24 hours to eliminate cross-tenant interference if the canary does not reduce error rate within 60 minutes (estimated cost: ~$3,200).
- Provision emergency SLA credit up to $12,000 if final impact meets our SLA policy thresholds (I will attach the computed outage minutes once fully baked).
- Fast-track a follow-up postmortem and a config guard to prevent prefix sharding changes without an automated heatmap check.

I recommend we:
1) Approve the temporary pool and instruct infra to stand up the pool immediately if the canary fails.
2) Assign Finance/Support the credit workflow (I've attached vectorio_request.pdf from their account team).
3) Schedule a 1:1 with Vectorio execs if they request — offer a formal incident update and remediation timeline.

Karthik will report canary metrics (miss rate, p99, error rate) in the incident doc. I will coordinate the credit path with Markus and Finance.

Evelyn Hart
Sr. Manager, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference
